label: Dub Audio
description: Dub a recording into another language: ElevenLabs translates it and re-voices it to match the original speakers. Runs as long as the dub takes and emits the dubbed audio (FLAC), even from a video.

inputs.name: account
inputs.description: The ElevenLabs access (wire an ElevenLabsAccess node).

inputs.name: file
inputs.description: The audio or video to dub, up to 3 GiB. Give this or `sourceUrl`, not both.

inputs.name: sourceUrl
inputs.label: Source link
inputs.description: If the recording is already online, give its public link here instead of `file`: ElevenLabs downloads it itself, so it never passes through weft. The same 3 GiB limit applies. Give this or `file`, not both.

inputs.name: targetLang
inputs.label: Target language
inputs.description: The language to dub into, as a code like `es` or `fr`, or a regional variant ElevenLabs supports, like `fr-CA` or `es-MX`.

inputs.name: sourceLang
inputs.label: Source language
inputs.description: The spoken language, as a code like `en`. Leave empty for ElevenLabs to detect it.

inputs.name: model
inputs.label: Model
inputs.description: dubbing_v1, the default, costs $0.50 a minute and dubs into 29 languages. If you want ElevenLabs's newer model, which it describes as "end-to-end dubbing that preserves voice and emotion", or one of the 92 languages it dubs into, pick dubbing_v2, at $2.20 a minute.

inputs.name: keyterms
inputs.description: Names and terms to get right in the transcription and the translation, like product or brand names. Up to 1,000, each at most 50 characters and 5 words, with none of the characters `<>{}[]\`.

inputs.name: cloningStrength
inputs.description: dubbing_v2 only. If you want the dubbed voices to copy the original speakers more or less closely, set 0 to 10; leave empty for ElevenLabs's default, 7. With it set, the node has to add your language after creating the project, so a language ElevenLabs does not dub is refused only after the project has cost one language's dub; left empty, such a language is refused before anything is charged. It cannot be combined with a `transcript` that carries translations.

inputs.name: transcript
inputs.description: Enterprise only. If you already have a transcript and want ElevenLabs to use it instead of transcribing the recording, give it here as a `{ "segments": [...] }` document of at most 20,000 segments and 4 MiB; for what goes in each segment, go and read ElevenLabs's guide Bring your own transcript (https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/dubbing/bring-your-own-transcript). It needs `sourceLang`. If one segment carries a `translation`, every segment must, and the dub uses those translations instead of machine translation; translations cannot be combined with `cloningStrength`.

inputs.name: reference
inputs.description: If you keep the project and want to recognize it on your side, put up to 500 characters here: ElevenLabs stores them on the project and gives them back unchanged. It does not change the dub. It needs `projectId` wired, since otherwise the node deletes the project.

outputs.name: file
outputs.description: The dubbed audio (FLAC), stored with the run and deleted with it (once the run's record goes); wire it through KeepFile to keep it past that.

outputs.name: projectId
outputs.description: The dub's project, on the ElevenLabs account whose key the node used. If it is your own account and you want to keep the project (to edit the dub or add languages to it in ElevenLabs), wire this. When nothing reads it, the node deletes the project once the dub is stored.

then.message: ElevenLabsDub '{id}' sets `cloningStrength`, which ElevenLabs offers only on dubbing_v2: set `model` to dubbing_v2, or leave `cloningStrength` empty.
ElevenLabsDub '{id}' gives a `transcript` with no `sourceLang`, and ElevenLabs needs to be told which language a transcript is in: set `sourceLang`.
ElevenLabsDub '{id}' sets a `reference` on a project it deletes once the dub is stored, because nothing reads `projectId`: wire `projectId` to keep the project, or leave `reference` empty.
ElevenLabsDub '{id}' gives both `file` and `sourceUrl`, and the dub takes its recording from one: keep one of them.
